# xCreen — open-source screen memory for macOS

**Open-source (Apache-2.0) screen memory for macOS that writes useful, source-linked insights into your Obsidian daily notes, powered by your own [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) and whichever models you configure.**

Looking for an open-source Rewind or Microsoft Recall alternative for Mac? xCreen is one, also comparable to Retrace, screenpipe and Goldfish, for people who already run Hermes Agent. [Website](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/) · [FAQ](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/faq/) · [Alternatives compared](https://al-ex-w.github.io/xCreen/alternatives/)

[![Verify](https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
[![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Platform: macOS 14+](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%2014%2B-lightgrey.svg)](INSTALL.md)

![xCreen menu-bar tray](docs/assets/tray.png)

<sub>The real tray view rendered offscreen with synthetic demo data (`scripts/render-screenshots.sh`); not a capture of anyone's screen.</sub>

> **Developer build.** Not notarized and not security-audited. Integrity (capture off) is ON by default.

## What it does

- **Menu-bar tray, Spotlight and CLI.** Ask questions about what you've seen from the tray, the macOS 26+ "Ask xCreen" Spotlight action or the "Search xCreen" row Spotlight offers under "Search in Apps" for any typed text (both fill the question in, you submit), or `xcreen ask` in a terminal.
- **Local capture with dedup.** Runs Apple Vision OCR on the foreground window at most once per second and drops text that is ≥90% similar to the last snapshot. Saves a screenshot every 10 active seconds.
- **Batches into one Hermes session.** Every 5 active minutes (or 30 images), a batch goes to a single persistent xCreen session in your Hermes Agent. It does not start a new chat each time.
- **Notes that read like yours.** The model first reads your vault's own conventions (e.g. `Agent/Vault Conventions.md`), then adds only what's worth remembering — decisions, deadlines, milestones, people, ideas — as plain bullets with `[[wikilinks]]` in that day's Daily note, and a dated line in a related existing project/person/organisation note when relevant. No page-by-page activity log and no ids or HTML comments in your notes; provenance (evidence ids, exact text, hashes) stays in xCreen's private journal. A batch with nothing worth noting writes nothing.
- **Integrity switch.** One switch, controlled only by you, stops all new screenshots and OCR. It is ON at first launch and keeps your choice across restarts.
- **7-day local retention, any model.** Raw evidence is deleted after seven days. You can pick any model your Hermes setup has configured. The default for the xCreen session is Claude Haiku 5.5 on your Anthropic account.

## xCreen vs alternatives

Facts come from each project's own public pages, checked October 2026 ([sources](#sources)). Products change, so check the linked pages yourself.

| | xCreen | Rewind | screenpipe | Retrace | Goldfish | Microsoft Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform | macOS 14+ | macOS[^rw1] | macOS, Windows, Linux[^sp1] | macOS 13+, Apple Silicon[^rt1] | macOS, Windows[^gf1] | Windows 11 Copilot+ PCs[^ms1] |
| License / source | Apache-2.0, open source | — | Source-available Screenpipe Commercial License; personal non-commercial use free, commercial use needs a license[^sp2] | MIT, open source[^rt2] | Not covered here | Windows feature |
| Capture method | Foreground-window screenshots + local Vision OCR | Screen and audio recording[^rw1] | Accessibility tree, OCR fallback, audio transcription[^sp1] | Screenshots every 2 s + Vision OCR, SQLite FTS5[^rt1] | Foreground-window text via Accessibility, no screenshots[^gf2] | Periodic snapshots[^ms1] |
| Where AI runs | Whichever provider your Hermes route uses (OCR is local, inference usually isn't) | — | Local models (e.g. Ollama) or cloud AI, as you configure[^sp1] | No model inference listed as active[^rt1] | Cloud: Azure OpenAI via Cloudflare; memory stored locally[^gf2] | Processed locally on the PC[^ms2] |
| Writes to your notes | Yes, sourced entries in Obsidian Daily notes | — | — | — | Keeps its own local memory, exposed over MCP[^gf2] | — |
| Status | Developer build | Shut down: capture disabled Dec 19, 2025 after Meta acquired Limitless[^rw1][^rw2] | Actively developed[^sp1] | "Very early development"[^rt1] | Free beta[^gf1] | Available on supported PCs[^ms1] |

"—" and "Not covered here" mean we did not check a primary source for that cell. Rewind's AI features are left out because the app has been discontinued.

## Requirements and who it's for

xCreen suits Mac users who already run Hermes Agent, keep notes in Obsidian, and are fine using a developer build.

- **A working [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) install is required.** xCreen does not include a model or keep API keys. It uses your Hermes profile read-only.
- **Local OCR does not mean local inference.** Batches and questions go to the provider behind your chosen route, and that provider's retention rules apply. For on-device inference, configure a local model in Hermes.
- **Developer build.** You build it from source with Swift/Xcode. It is not notarized. Use a stable signing identity so macOS keeps the Screen Recording permission across reinstalls.
- macOS 14 or later, Xcode/Swift and Python 3. The Spotlight action needs macOS 26 or later and full Xcode (its App Intents metadata tool); launch xCreen once after installing so Spotlight can index it, which may take a minute.

## Quick start

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen.git && cd xCreen
bash scripts/install.sh           # builds, installs to ~/Applications, copies `xcreen` to ~/.local/bin
xcreen status                     # Integrity should report ON (capture paused)
```

Turn Integrity OFF from the tray when you want capture to start. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for vault setup, signing, verification and uninstalling.

## Privacy and safety

- **What's captured** (only while Integrity is OFF and the Mac is unlocked and awake): screenshots and OCR text of the eligible foreground window.
- **Where it's stored:** in private files under `~/Library/Application Support/xCreen`, outside your vault and outside this repository. This storage is not encrypted, so use FileVault. Only short distilled bullets go into your vault; their evidence links live in the private receipt journal under `~/.hermes/xcreen-receipts`, not in notes.
- **Retention:** raw evidence expires after 7 days. Anything already sent to your model provider or saved in Hermes history follows their retention rules. Deletion does not guarantee forensic erasure.
- **Excluded:** known password managers (1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, KeePass, Apple Passwords, Keychain), System Settings, lock and login screens, and xCreen itself.
- **NOT protected:** browser password fields, password-manager browser extensions and popovers, and incognito/private windows are **not detected or redacted**. Turn Integrity ON before sensitive browsing.
- **Vault writes are confined:** Markdown only, inside existing vault folders; never `Agent/`, `Archive/`, templates or hidden folders (`.obsidian`), never outside the vault, bounded size, and xCreen never deletes or rewrites your text (it only adds lines or revises lines it wrote itself).
- **Integrity is user-only:** only your tray or CLI action changes it. The model and screen content cannot turn capture on. Screen text is treated as untrusted evidence, never as instructions.

Full rules and limits: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) · [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md).

## CLI

```sh
xcreen status
xcreen ask "What was the error I saw in the build log this morning?"
xcreen integrity on
xcreen models list
xcreen batches
```

Full command list and semantics: [docs/cli.md](docs/cli.md).

# Installing xCreen

Requires macOS 14+, Xcode/Swift and Python 3, plus an installed [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) (check with `hermes --print-runtime-command`). xCreen uses your Hermes profile read-only and sends inference to whichever provider your selected route uses; local OCR does not make inference local. Do not edit Hermes auth/config, grant screen permissions, enable capture, inspect private vault contents or run inference to verify installation.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen.git
cd xCreen
bash scripts/install.sh --no-launch
```

The installer obtains Hermes's Python/source root from its official launcher, locates an optional vault using `OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH` or Obsidian metadata, builds and copies the app to `~/Applications`, pre-fills settings, and copies the standalone Python CLI to `~/.local/bin/xcreen`. Add that directory to PATH. `--vault "/absolute/vault/path"` overrides detection. Omit `--no-launch` to launch. Integrity defaults ON; a saved explicit preference is restored, but actual capture stays blocked until current safety gates pass. Startup never requests permissions.

The copied CLI and bundled runtime do not depend on the checkout. The installer uses a configured `XCREEN_SIGN_IDENTITY`, otherwise an available Apple Development identity, otherwise ad-hoc signing. This is not a notarized consumer release. A stable signing identity is needed to preserve grants across reinstalls.

## Verify without capture or inference

```sh
xcreen start
xcreen status
xcreen integrity get
xcreen session visibility get
xcreen settings show
xcreen models list
xcreen logs --no-follow
```

Status is read directly from the running app, not a stale file. It must report Integrity true and capture paused. Connecting/model inventory resumes only the dedicated xCreen session and runs no model request. If Hermes cannot connect, the CLI returns an error and the tray shows the connection failure; no answer is claimed. Avoid publishing local settings/log output because it may contain personal paths or identifiers.

## Change settings through the owner

```sh
xcreen settings set python /absolute/python3
xcreen settings set root /absolute/hermes-agent
xcreen settings set vault "/absolute/vault"
xcreen settings set vault "" # disables Daily-note writing
xcreen settings autodetect
xcreen connection reconnect
xcreen model default                       # show the xCreen session default
xcreen model select PROVIDER EXACT_MODEL_ID # also saves it as the xCreen default
```

Settings are persisted by the running app and its gateway reconnects; session identity is retained. The xCreen session default is Claude Haiku 5.5 on your Anthropic account (`anthropic` / `claude-haiku-5-5`) until you pick another configured route in the tray or with `xcreen model default PROVIDER MODEL`; it applies only to the xCreen session, never Hermes's global default, and an unavailable model is reported rather than replaced. Do not use `defaults write` as a parallel live control surface. The installer pre-fills defaults only while the app is stopped.

## User-only deliberate actions
The **Show session in Hermes** tray toggle defaults OFF (hidden). Use `xcreen session visibility on` or `off` to change that same persisted preference for the existing xCreen session. Offline changes remain pending until connection/resume applies them. `xcreen --json status` separates desired `sessionVisible`, last gateway-confirmed `actualSessionVisible` (absent when unknown), and `sessionVisibilityPending`. No profile defaults, session identity, Integrity preference or capture behavior change. Upgrading an existing install with no saved visibility preference applies hidden on its next connection, even if the session was previously manually unhidden.

- Integrity OFF in the tray or `xcreen integrity off` explicitly consents to capture. The same actual service runs permission/state/exclusion gates for both interfaces. Permission denial leaves the user's desired switch unchanged and reports capture blocked; an explicit OFF action may show macOS's permission/settings UI. Do not bypass it. No development test should execute this action against a real capture service.
- `xcreen ask "QUESTION"` explicitly authorizes that question in the xCreen session. Captured evidence can reach a model provider, and Hermes/provider history may outlive local seven-day retention.
- Configuring a vault enables the scoped source-bound writer for existing Daily notes; do not configure it without understanding that boundary.
- On macOS 26+, Spotlight offers "Ask xCreen" (asks for a question, then opens the panel with it filled in; you submit) and "Open xCreen". The build fails if Xcode's App Intents metadata lacks these App Shortcuts. Spotlight picks them up after the installed app is registered and launched once; indexing can take a minute and ranking is up to macOS.

## Uninstall

```sh
xcreen stop
rm -rf ~/Applications/xCreen.app
rm -f ~/.local/bin/xcreen
defaults delete dev.xcreen.app
```

Optionally remove `~/Library/Application Support/xCreen`, `~/Library/Logs/xCreen`, and `~/.xcreen-control` after stopping. This does not delete Hermes history, vault notes, backups or provider retention.

See the [CLI reference](docs/cli.md), [CLI parity](docs/cli-parity.md) and [implementation limits](docs/implementation-progress.md).

<!-- source: https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md -->

# How xCreen works

This page holds the pipeline and boundary details. For the design, see [architecture](architecture.md); for the commands, see the [CLI reference](cli.md).

## Capture pipeline

When Integrity is explicitly turned OFF and every safety gate permits it:

1. The foreground window is sampled for local Apple Vision OCR at most once per eligible second.
2. OCR that is ≥90% similar to the last saved snapshot is discarded.
3. Independent screenshots are saved every ten active seconds.
4. Five active minutes (or 30 images) form a durable batch, sent with timestamp/ID binding to the same dedicated xCreen Hermes session.
5. Private evidence files stay outside the vault (under `~/Library/Application Support/xCreen`) and expire after seven days. No forensic-erasure or database-encryption claim is made; use FileVault.

Integrity defaults ON and the user's explicitly chosen value is preserved across restart. Only explicit tray/CLI actions change it. Lock, sleep, exclusions, missing permissions and errors suspend capture without rewriting that choice.

## Hermes runtime and tools

The bundled Hermes runtime registers only the scoped xCreen tools:

- latest/range OCR listing and timestamped coverage status
- OCR search and nearby image lookup
- native image loading
- read-only vault access (`xcreen_vault_read`, `xcreen_vault_list`) so the model can follow the vault's own conventions note and link existing notes
- a note writer (`xcreen_note_write`) when a vault is configured

The model writes like the user: short plain bullets with `[[wikilinks]]`, only for valuable items (decisions, commitments, milestones, things learned, people, ideas), never a log of apps or pages. A batch with nothing worth noting writes nothing and is recorded as skipped. Besides the capture-date Daily note it may add a dated bullet under a section of an existing note (e.g. `Projects/X.md`) or, sparingly, create a note in an existing folder.

Write safety: vault-relative `.md` paths only, inside existing non-hidden folders; `Agent/`, `Archive/`, `Sources/`, templates, attachments, `.obsidian` and the vault root are refused; Daily writes go only to the capture-date note; bounded size per write; no-follow directory walk, hardlink/symlink rejection, atomic replace with a concurrent-change check. xCreen never deletes or rewrites user text: it inserts lines, or replaces a line it wrote itself (`revises`). Text with HTML comments, evidence ids or long hashes is rejected.

Provenance lives outside the vault in xCreen's private receipt journal (`$HERMES_HOME/xcreen-receipts/`): batch id, note path, exact inserted text, its hash, the note's pre-write hash and evidence ids. Retries check the journal and whether the exact text is already present, so they never duplicate; edited or removed bullets become `uncertain` and are never re-added. `scripts/migrate-vault-notes.py --vault … [--dry-run]` moves the markup of older xCreen versions (`<!-- xcreen-entry … -->`) out of Daily notes into this journal.

Native automatic turns prepare an immutable host-validated batch binding and complete only after explicit saved/skipped model results and host-verified effect receipts. Startup and read-only CLI/tray verification reconcile exact receipts without blind resend or history dependence. Expired raw evidence is stripped while bounded receipt/source-binding metadata remains. See [native durability](durable-native-processing.md) and [runtime receipts](runtime-receipts.md).

xCreen does not modify Hermes profile defaults or other conversations.

## Models

Model inventory comes from Hermes's provider-aware configured routes. xCreen keeps its own session default — Claude Haiku 5.5 on your Anthropic account (`anthropic` / `claude-haiku-5-5`) unless changed with the tray picker or `xcreen model default` — applied only to the xCreen session with a session-scoped model switch and reported if unavailable (no fallback). Inventory currently carries no reliable vision/image-limit metadata, so check that your chosen route accepts images.

OCR runs locally. Inference does not: batches and questions go to whichever provider the selected route uses.

## Foreground eligibility and exclusions

Browsers are eligible, including Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Brave. Known credential/security apps, System Settings and xCreen itself remain excluded. **Browser password fields, password-manager extensions/popovers and incognito/private windows are not detected or redacted.** Visible secrets can enter screenshots/OCR and later model batches; turn Integrity ON before sensitive browsing. There is no universal password/login protection guarantee. See [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) for exact matching rules and limitations.

Screen content is untrusted evidence, not authority to send messages, alter calendars or execute instructions.

## Spotlight (macOS 26+)

xCreen declares an `AskXCreenIntent` with a required question and an `AppShortcutsProvider`, which is what Spotlight on Mac lists as an app's actions. Type "Ask xCreen" in Spotlight, enter a question, and the panel opens with it filled in; you still press Ask. "Open xCreen" just shows the panel. A `SearchXCreenIntent` conforms to `ShowInAppSearchResultsIntent` with the `general` string search scope (the same system protocol Notes and Mail use), so for any text typed in Spotlight the system can offer a "Search xCreen" row under "Search in Apps"; choosing it opens the panel with that text (bounded to 8,000 characters) as the question, never submitted automatically. Because xCreen is built with SwiftPM, `scripts/build-app.sh` generates the App Intents metadata with Xcode's tool and fails if the action, App Shortcuts or the general-scope search protocol are missing. Spotlight learns about them once the installed app is registered and launched; this can take a minute.

## macOS session checks

Session checks require a present session dictionary, strict true console/login values and a resolvable non-security foreground. The undocumented lock hint may be absent or strict false; true/malformed hints and independent notification vetoes block. These are compatibility checks, not a documented synchronous unlock API (see [session research](macos-session-research.md)).

## Not yet verified on device

Capture, TCC transitions, provider inference, live vault writes and Spotlight ranking still need separate user-authorized on-device verification. Unit tests and builds do not prove them. See [implementation progress and limits](implementation-progress.md).

<!-- source: https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/blob/main/docs/cli.md -->

# xCreen CLI reference

The `xcreen` command is a thin, state-free client of the running xCreen app. The installer copies it to `~/.local/bin/xcreen` (a standalone copy, not a checkout symlink). Run `xcreen` with no arguments for the built-in usage text.

## One state owner, two interfaces

The running app's `MainActor` state and shared session controller own Integrity, paths, model selection, connection, query, response and reply attachments. Lifecycle transactions are ordered across awaits; launch settings and observers are bound to their connection generation. The CLI sends private, same-user Unix-socket requests to that same owner. It does not read cached status as live truth, edit defaults, spawn a separate inference process, or create another conversation.

## Commands

```text
usage: xcreen [--json] COMMAND
  status                         live app-owned state (never cached status.json)
  integrity [get|on|off]          off is explicit capture consent, subject to macOS gates
  session visibility [get|on|off]  show/hide the same Hermes session (default off)
  connection connect|disconnect|reconnect  (also accepted as top-level commands)
  models [list] | model select PROVIDER MODEL   (select also saves the xCreen default)
  model default [get] | model default PROVIDER MODEL  xCreen-session default only
  settings [show] | settings set python|root|vault VALUE
  settings autodetect | autodetect
  ask QUESTION [--wait-ms 0..30000]  explicit submission to the existing xCreen session
  history [--after CURSOR]        bounded sanitized history pages
  batches [--after BATCH_ID]      up to 20 durable batch metadata records
  batches retry                   verify, then re-queue only receipt-proven zero-effect batches
  verify                         read-only receipt reconciliation; no inference/note writes
  cancel
  images [list|open ID]           reply attachment metadata/open through the app
  panel [show|hide]
  start | stop | restart | quit
  logs [-n N] [--no-follow] [--gateway]
```

Examples:

```sh
xcreen status
xcreen --json status
xcreen integrity get
xcreen integrity on
xcreen session visibility get
xcreen connection reconnect
xcreen models list
xcreen model default
xcreen model select PROVIDER EXACT_MODEL_ID
xcreen settings show
xcreen settings set vault ""        # disables Daily-note writing
xcreen settings autodetect
xcreen ask "Summarize my recent context" --wait-ms 30000
xcreen history
xcreen batches
xcreen verify
xcreen cancel
xcreen images list
xcreen images open IMAGE_ID
xcreen panel show
xcreen logs --no-follow
xcreen start
xcreen stop
xcreen restart
```

## Semantics

**Integrity.** `xcreen integrity off` is an explicit user capture-consent action, equivalent to the tray switch. A denied safety gate leaves the requested switch OFF but capture suspended/blocked with its reason. Lock, sleep and errors never change the user's switch. Startup does not request permissions. Never run OFF as an automated installation/test step. Integrity ON does not erase history or block deliberate historical questions.

**ask.** Submits once to the existing xCreen session. Waiting is bounded to 30 seconds; expiry does **not** cancel an admitted turn. Use `history` or `cancel`. Ask, history and model inventory may reconnect the dedicated session; connection failures are explicit.

**cancel.** Targets the admitted manual question, including a question queued behind automatic work, not an unrelated automatic turn.

**history.** Comes from the host's `xcreen.history.page` for the exact resumed runtime session, not a second transcript database. `history [--after CURSOR]` returns sanitized stable snapshot pages bounded before gateway stdout, flags oversized messages and removes image pixels. Evicted/restarted host cursors fail explicitly.

**batches / verify.** `batches [--after BATCH_ID]` lists up to 20 byte-bounded processing-state and actual receipt metadata records, also visible in the tray; continue from the last ID until an empty page. `xcreen verify` and the tray's Verify receipts action reconcile exact host receipts without inference or note writes. `batches retry` verifies first and re-queues only batches whose host receipt proves zero effects; it does not send inference itself. See [native durability](durable-native-processing.md).

**images.** `images list|open` covers the current answer's resolved attachment IDs, not arbitrary paths or a general filesystem browser.

**model.** `models list` shows Hermes's provider-aware configured routes. `model select` and `model default PROVIDER MODEL` set the xCreen session default only (built-in default: `anthropic` / `claude-haiku-5-5`); Hermes's global default is unchanged. An unavailable model is reported; there is no silent fallback.

**settings.** Changes are persisted by the running app and report persistence and reconnect failure separately. Do not use `defaults write` as a parallel live control surface.

**session visibility.** The tray's **Show session in Hermes** switch and `xcreen session visibility [get|on|off]` share one app-owned persisted preference, default **OFF (hidden)**. They update the existing active session, never create another conversation or change profile defaults. Connect/resume reapplies the saved preference. Offline changes are saved and reported **pending**, separately from gateway-confirmed visibility; they do not connect automatically. `xcreen --json status` separates desired `sessionVisible`, last gateway-confirmed `actualSessionVisible` (absent when unknown), and `sessionVisibilityPending`. This switch does not affect Integrity or capture.

**Argument handling.** Global `--json` goes before the command; option-shaped question/setting values stay literal.

**start / stop.** Start launches the installed app without enabling capture; stop/quit request graceful app-owned teardown. No process-name kill is used by the CLI.

**URL scheme and Spotlight.** `xcreen://ask?query=...`, `xcreen://open` and the macOS 26+ "Ask xCreen"/"Open xCreen" App Shortcuts only open/fill the panel, never submit automatically. They work whether xCreen is already running or is launched by the URL. Arbitrary-query Spotlight interception is not claimed.

See [CLI/tray parity](cli-parity.md) for acknowledgment, lineage and security limits.


---

<!-- source: https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/blob/main/SECURITY.md -->

# Security and privacy

Developer build, not security-audited or notarized. The native capture pipeline is connected; this is not a disconnected UI preview. Integrity defaults ON only when no explicit preference exists and preserves the user's chosen preference. Only explicit user actions change it. Permission/session/app gates can suspend capture without changing that preference. Integrity ON blocks new screenshots/OCR and automatic transmission; it does not erase retained evidence or provider history, or block deliberate historical questions.

## Foreground exclusions and their limits

Browsers are eligible, including Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc and Orion. **Browser password fields, password-manager extensions/popovers and incognito/private windows are not detected or redacted.** There is no page/URL, Accessibility secure-field, private-mode or secret-content detector in the native capture path. Vision recognizes text; it does not sanitize secrets. Masked password dots are not a protection supplied by xCreen. Visible credentials, recovery codes, autofill menus and login pages can enter screenshots/OCR and later automatic model batches. Turn Integrity ON before sensitive activity. There is no universal password/login protection guarantee.

`ForegroundCapturePolicy` compares lowercase bundle IDs:

- Exact exclusions: `dev.xcreen.app`, `com.apple.passwords`, `com.apple.systemsettings`, `com.apple.systempreferences`, `com.agilebits.onepassword7`.
- Conservative substring exclusions: `1password`, `bitwarden`, `lastpass`, `dashlane`, `keepass`, `keychain`, `loginwindow`, `screenlock`, `securityagent`, `screensaver`, `lockscreen`. These cover variants but can also block unrelated apps whose IDs contain these strings. Exact exclusions do not extend to arbitrary IDs that merely contain the full exact ID.
- Missing/empty foreground identity or invalid PID prevents capture. This is an identifier policy, not signature verification or exhaustive knowledge of all credential apps. Embedded extensions/overlays are not independently classified; an excluded app must be the observed foreground app for this gate to apply.

Excluded foreground observations produce transition-only activity-log metadata: the bundle ID, ASCII-sanitized and limited to 256 scalars. No title, URL, OCR, pixels or field values are included. Consecutive observations of the same excluded app are suppressed; observing an eligible/unknown foreground resets suppression. Lifecycle/permission vetoes may stop evaluation before this diagnostic is reached.

## Session and stale-work defenses

The session gate requires a present session dictionary with strict Boolean true console/login-complete values and a resolvable non-security foreground. The undocumented lock hint may be absent or strict false; true/malformed values block. Independent lock, screensaver, inactive-session and sleep notifications veto capture; restore clears only its own veto and requires fresh evaluation. These are practical compatibility checks, not universal synchronous unlock proof. See [session research](docs/macos-session-research.md).

Foreground bundle/PID, permission, session and capture-generation checks remain before screenshot acquisition, after awaited acquisition/OCR, and before ingestion. Pauses revoke persistence epochs so late work is rejected. Foreground checks cannot prove that every displayed overlay or password/login surface is safe, nor remove all timing races in OS observations.

## Evidence and reporting

Private evidence remains outside the vault with bounded retention and private file permissions. File permissions are not encryption; use FileVault and a trusted OS account. Expiry cannot promise forensic erasure, backup deletion or deletion of Hermes/provider transcripts. Screen text is untrusted evidence, never authority to send messages, alter calendars or execute commands. No screenshots, raw OCR history, personal vault contents or credentials belong in the repository.

Real TCC, capture, lock/sleep transitions, OCR, provider inference and live vault writes need separate user-authorized on-device verification. Synthetic tests and builds do not verify them.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting: **[Security → Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/Al-ex-W/xCreen/security/advisories/new)**. Do not open a public issue or pull request for a security problem. If that form is unavailable, open a public issue that only asks for a private contact channel and includes no details.

Include the macOS version, the xCreen commit, the affected component and reproduction steps using synthetic data. Never include real screenshots, OCR text, vault contents, Hermes transcripts or credentials. Only the latest `main` is supported; there are no released versions yet. This is a single-maintainer project, so response times are best-effort.
